title: Mingus on the red car and his bossing of pianists
summary: Buddy Collette's story of Mingus playing on the streetcar leads her to repeat that he bugged piano players.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Buddy Collette tells a story that Mingus used to get into his playing so much that he couldn't quit to go take a streetcar ride to a job or something, and so he would take his bass on the red car and play on the red car. And so Buddy said sometimes, he said, 'As long as Mingus was playing, I'd take out my flute or something, or one of my horns, and we'd play on the red car. Passengers seemed to enjoy it.'
He was a character, there's no question
about it. He was quite a character.
You never got in on any of Mingus's streetcar concerts.

No, no, no, no. As I say, the only time I ever worked with him, really, was at the Downbeat, you know. I worked with him there. It was a couple of nights or so, and well, it was an experience that, really, I wouldn't have wanted to work with him too much, because he was a bug as far as a piano player was concerned, you know, and his conception of what should be done, what should be played chord-wise, you know, it was just altogether different from what I would have done, you know. But this is the type of a musician he was, you know, and I imagine he did this to any piano player, because I've talked to other piano players that have worked with him. He was the type of guy that would dictate to the person, you know, what to do and what to play, the piano player particularly. He didn't bother anybody else, but he was on a piano player.
